title: FIRPTA: the buyer withholds 15% when a foreign person sells U.S. real property
rule: When a foreign person disposes of a U.S. real property interest, the buyer generally must withhold 15% of the amount realized, counting cash, other property at market value, and debt assumed or taken subject to. No withholding is needed if the seller certifies under penalty of perjury its U.S. taxpayer identification number and non-foreign status, unless the buyer knows otherwise. A buyer that fails to withhold can be liable; Form 8288 is generally due by the 20th day after transfer.
changeWatch: Changes to section 1445 or its regulations, and to IRS Forms 8288 and 8288-A or their filing rules.

sources.title: 26 U.S.C. 1445, Withholding of tax on dispositions of United States real property interests
sources.quote: the transferee shall be required to deduct and withhold a tax equal to 15 percent of the amount realized on the disposition

sources.title: FIRPTA withholding
sources.quote: If the transferor is a foreign person and the transferee fails to withhold, the transferee may be held liable for the tax.

sources.title: Reporting and paying tax on U.S. real property interests
sources.quote: Generally, transferees must file Form 8288 by the 20th day after the date of the disposition.
